name: לְחִי
summary: Lehi is a place in Judah where the Philistines spread out against Samson and where he struck them with a donkey’s jawbone. The name is the noun לְחִי “jaw, jawbone”, and Judges 15 plays on it: Samson calls the place Ramath-lehi.

evidence.note: The Philistines camp in Judah and spread out at Lehi.
Samson finds a fresh donkey’s jawbone, לְחִי, and strikes a thousand men with it.
After throwing away the jawbone, Samson calls the place Ramath-lehi.
The narrator locates the spring En-hakkore in Lehi.

note: Moved from the name word of the former one-word entry for לְחִי; the common noun “jaw, cheek” is in the root entry לחה, which this name links to. Judges 15 plays on the shared sound of the place name and the common noun. The narrative already calls the site Lehi before Samson finds the bone and explicitly connects his act with the longer name Ramath-lehi. The ancient name of the settlement before this episode is uncertain.
